text.p: Align-Rite International Inc said on Tuesday that it has signed a photomask supply contract with Philips Semiconductor Group which will cover 90 percent of its photomask requirements until 1999.
The financial value of the contract was not disclosed.
Philips Semiconductor Group, based in Stockport, England, is a subsidiary of Philips Electronics NV.
DuPont Photomasks Inc, a rival manufacturer of photomasks, said it did not believe the contract affected its own relationship with Philips Semiconductor.

"The announcement has no believed implications on DuPont Photomask's relationship and business with Philips Semiconductor's global operations," said Chief Financial Officer David Gino in a telephone conversation with Reuters.
"We believe that this is business that Align-Rite currently has, not business that is captured away from DuPont," he added.
DuPont Photomask's shares were at 48-1/8 in late-morning trading, down 1-5/8 from their close at 49-3/4 on Friday but up from the opening price of 46-1/2.
Align-Rite's shares were up one at 13.

Photomasks are high-purity quartz or glass plates containing microscopic images of integrated circuits and are used as masters by semiconductor manufacturers to optically transfer the circuit images onto semiconductor wafers.

Elliott Rogers, an analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said that Align-Rite had a strong relationship with Philips and the announcement on Tuesday constituted, in effect, an "extension of their business contract with the Philips subsidiary."
It did not necessarily translate into increased market share and should have "zero impact" on DuPont, he said.
Meanwhile, he said, "the air pocket in DuPont's stock turned out to be a splendid buying opportunity."
